full_judgment:
2. This Rule was issued, at the instance of accused-petitioner Tareq Shamsul Khan alias Himu and three others, calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the order dated 6-2-2003 passed by the Judge of  Druta Bichar Tribunal, Dhaka Division, Dhaka, in Druta Bichar Tribunal Case No.1 of 2003 arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 39 (2) 01 and GR No. 411 of 2001, should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. Mr Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that as many as four first information reports were lodged over self-same occurrence stating different issues thereto against some unknown persons and police ultimately submitted charge-sheets. He then submits that Motijheel PS Case No. 38 dated 13-2- 2001 was started for the alleged offence under sections 326/307/302/34 of the Penal Code without naming any person as accused in the column of the first information report. He then submits that another first information report was lodged against unknown accused for the alleged offence under sections 326/307/302/34 of the Penal Code over self-same occurrence. He further submits that on self-same occurrence another first information report was lodged on the self-same date mentioning the time of occurrence same as of two others against some unknown persons which was registered as Motijheel PS Case No. 39(1)01 while one Moazzem Hossain as informant lodged a first information report against a particular person along with others alleging the offence under the aforesaid sections of law which was tagged with Motijheel PS Case No. 39 dated 13-2-2001, as it relates to same fact and incident. He then submits that Ramna PS Case No. 35 dated 13-3-2001 under sections 10 and 12 of Jana Nirapatta (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 2000, against Mirza Abbas and six others having been started, the case was transferred to Jana Nirapatta Bighnakari Oporadh Daman Tribunal being Jana Nirapatta Case No. 81 of 2001 which was challenged by Writ Petition No. 657 of 2001 before the High Court Division on 27th February, 2001 and obtained Rule with an ad-interim order to the effect that not to arrest, harass or disturb the accused. It is further submitted that Motijheel PS Case No. 38(2) 2001 had ended in charge-sheet against Mirza Abbas and others which has been challenged under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the High Court Division has been pleased to issue Rule and stay all further proceedings of the case and, in continuation of his submission, he submits that since all the aforesaid three cases arise out of same cause of action and the parties are almost same inasmuch as alamats of the cases are common in such circumstances it is convenient to dispose of all these three cases simultaneously treating the same as counter-cases. He lastly submits that if the present case be tried separately, the accused-petitioners may be prejudiced, since the present case is the counter case of other two cases as mentioned above and in the circumstances he submits that for ends of justice as well as to avoid any future complication the present case should be tried one after another along with other two cases which are, no doubt, counter-cases of the present one as per law. 

 5. As against this, the learned Deputy Attorney General opposes the Rule contending, inter alia, that one of the petitioners, namely, Tareq Shamsul Khan alias Himu only moved as application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the learned trial Court, but other accused-petitioners in joint petition moved this criminal revision which proves their joint ill motive to stay the proceedings in Druta Bichar Tribunal Case being No. 1 of 2003 pending before the learned Judge of Druta Bichar Tribunal, Dhaka Division, Dhaka arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 39 dated 23-2-2001 corresponding to GR No. 411 of 2001 under sections 147/149/323/326/307/302/34 of the Penal Code and accordingly, he contends that the Rule is liable to be discharged. He further submits that the proceedings of the Tribunal Case has been stayed till disposal of the Rule, but the matter has been extended again till disposal of the Rule on 25-6-2003 by suppressing the non-submission of the copy of notice which is illegal and thus the Rule has become infructuous. He then submits that the facts and circumstances of the present case in no way comes under the mischief of section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that the merit of the aforesaid three cases are to be decided at the time of trial and the subject matter being not same of these three cases, the present case may not be treated as counter-case of others as mentioned earlier and he lastly, submits that the petitioners by amalgamating all the aforesaid police station cases mentioned above are trying to delay the proceedings of the trial Court and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 6. Paragraph 15 of the counter-affidavit so filed by the opposite-party-State admits the fact that Ramna PS Case No. 35(2) 2001 is a counter-case to the case which has been challenged in this proceeding and after-thought of the accused of Motijheel PS Case No. 39(2) 2001. So, it is not befitting to state that the present case is independent to that of Motijheel PS Case No. 39(2) 2001-the proceedings of which has been stayed by this Court in this criminal revision. As a general rule adjournment should not be granted unless necessitates in the interest of justice. We have already mentioned earlier that the present case has been admitted to be the counter-case of another case of Motijheel Police Station whose proceedings has been stayed by this Court and in such circumstances it cannot be ruled out that the decision of this case may influence the other cases which have got same date of occurrence as well as fact. In such circumstances it is desirable that for ends of justice as well as to avoid any future complication all the aforesaid three counter-cases should be tried by same Judge one after another which may not prejudice the parties and, in view of such facts and circumstances, we are constrained to hold that the petitioners have got cogent ground to seek adjournment in this case inasmuch as the provision of section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is very much applicable in the instant case. We are, at the same time, aware about the fate of all these cases and in such circumstances the parties may be directed to get the other two cases (one writ petition and a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure pending before this Court) disposed of at their personal initiative as early as possible. Since it has been admitted that the present case is a counter-case of other two so mentioned earlier; we find cogent reason to entertain this application. 

 7. Accordingly, the Rule issued earlier is made absolute and the impugned order, dated 6-2-2003, passed by the learned Judge, Druta Bichar Tribunal, Dhaka Division, Dhaka, in Druta Bichar Tribunal Case No.1 of 2003 arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 39(2)2001 corresponding to GR No. 411 of 2001, rejecting the application of the petitioners under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, is set aside.
